description: Fetch property claims for a Wikidata entity with qualifier and reference detail. Item QIDs and quantity units — in values, qualifiers, and references — are resolved to human-readable labels by default, and every P-ID the statements name comes back labelled in propertyLabels. Each property returns up to limit statements (default 10) starting at offset, in upstream order; propertyTotals counts every statement each property holds, and nextOffset, present while any property holds more, continues every property at once. Use the properties parameter to fetch only specific P-IDs — omitting it returns every property, and a well-connected item (a country, a major city) carries hundreds of them: more than fits inline. A page of several properties over 24,000 bytes before labels comes back as kind: "outline" — every P-ID on the page with its byte size, largest first — instead of the statements; re-call with the same id, limit, offset, and rank plus properties:[...] naming P-IDs whose sizes sum to 24,000 or less (the retrieval_notice names one such set). Labels are added after that check, so a returned page can run past 24,000 bytes by their size, and a single property is never outlined: it returns its window whatever the size. Designed for fact verification: "what does Wikidata say about this entity's {property}?". For a current value, rank: "best" keeps each property's preferred statements, or its normal ones when none is preferred, and never deprecated ones — the statements SPARQL's wdt: reads. Check qualifiers and references for temporal scope and evidence.

id.description: Q-ID (e.g., "Q76") or P-ID of the entity to fetch statements for, bare or as an entity URI or wd: form (e.g., "http://www.wikidata.org/entity/Q76", "wd:Q76").

language.description: Wikidata language code for label resolution of QID values and P-IDs (e.g., "en", "de"). Case-insensitive; "_" is read as "-"; blank means "en".

limit.description: Statements returned per property, starting at offset, in upstream order. Default 10; a larger value returns at most 500 per property and says so.

offset.description: Statements skipped in each property before its window. Start at 0; pass the nextOffset a response returns to continue every property at once.

properties.description: P-IDs to fetch (e.g., ["P31", "P569", "P27"]), bare or as an entity URI or wd: form. Omit to return all properties (may be large for major items).

rank.description: Which statements each property keeps. "all" keeps every statement, deprecated ones included. "best" keeps a property's preferred statements when it has any, otherwise its normal ones, and never deprecated ones — the truthy statements SPARQL's wdt: reads. Applied before every count, the limit/offset window, the outline check, and labels.

resolve_labels.description: Resolve item QIDs (label), quantity unit QIDs (unitLabel), and the P-IDs of statements, qualifiers, reference parts, and property-typed values (propertyLabels) to human-readable labels via one batched label call over the returned statements. Set to false to skip label resolution and return raw IDs only (faster, smaller payload).

name: wikidata_get_statements

error.description: Present when the call failed. Absent on success.

code.description: JSON-RPC error code for this failure.

reason.description: Machine-readable failure mode. Declared by this tool: `entity_not_found`: No entity exists at this ID — either unassigned or out of range. `invalid_id`: ID is not a valid Q-ID or P-ID format. `invalid_property`: A properties entry is not a valid P-ID format. Other values are possible when a failure originates below the handler.

recovery.description: Actionable next step for the caller.

message.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong.

id.description: The entity ID whose statements were fetched.

kind.description: full — statements carries the claims. outline — the statement set overflowed the inline byte budget, so sections lists the P-IDs available instead; re-call with properties:[...] to retrieve specific ones. The counts below are reported either way.

labelsResolved.description: True when the returned statements had labels resolved: resolve_labels was true and kind is full, so every item QID and quantity unit that resolved carries its label, and propertyLabels holds every P-ID that resolved. False when resolve_labels was false, on an outline, which carries no statements and makes no label lookup, and when the label service did not answer, which the notice says.

nextOffset.description: Present in full mode while any property holds statements past this window: offset + limit. Re-call with offset: nextOffset to continue every property at once. Absent on the last page, and on an outline: re-call for this window first.

notice.description: Present when limit was above the per-call cap of 500 (the requested and applied values), when offset is past the end of every property (the largest total), when rank "best" kept no statement of a property because all of them are deprecated (those properties and how to read them), or when the label service did not answer, so the statements came back unlabelled.

propertyCount.description: Number of distinct properties — those returned in full mode, those offered as sections in outline mode.

propertyLabels.description: P-ID → label in language for the properties the returned statements name: statement keys, qualifier and reference-part properties, and property-typed values. Present when labelsResolved is true; a P-ID with no label is absent and renders bare.

propertyTotals.description: Statements each property in the selection holds after the rank filter and before the window, keyed by P-ID — 0 for a property whose statements are all deprecated under rank "best". Lists a property paged past its end too. Reported in both modes.

retrieval_notice.description: Present when kind = outline: how to re-call for specific properties.

returnedCount.description: Statements returned in statements, across every property — this page. 0 on an outline.

sections.description: Present when kind = outline: the P-IDs with statements in this limit/offset window, largest first, each sized as the UTF-8 bytes its window adds to a response before labels. Sizes add up: copy names whose sizes sum to 24,000 or less into the properties input, with the same limit, offset, and rank, to retrieve them.

items.description: An available property — its P-ID and the serialized byte size of its statements in this window.

bytes.description: Serialized byte size of the section

name.description: Section identifier — pass in `sections` to retrieve it

statementCount.description: Statements across every property in the selection, after the rank filter and before the limit/offset window and any overflow, so it reports the full volume the rank keeps in both modes.

statements.description: Map of property ID to array of normalized statements. Each statement has id, rank, property, value (with type-specific fields), optional qualifiers ([{ property, value }]), and optional references — one entry per source in upstream order, each { parts: [{ property, value }] }. Present in full mode; omitted in outline mode.

truncated.description: True when the window cut at least one property short of its total: nextOffset continues it. Absent otherwise.

title: Get Wikidata Statements
